intended_object: The degree-n integral singular homology functor X ↦ H_n(X; ℤ) from topological spaces to ℤ-modules (abelian groups). This comes from the docstring and the name; the definition is an alias of `AlgebraicTopology.integralSingularHomologyFunctor`.
explanation: The body is `integralSingularHomologyFunctor n`, which is defined as `(singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u,0} ℤ) n).obj integerCoefficients`. Here `integerCoefficients` is ℤ as a ℤ-module, lifted to universe u with `ModuleCat.uliftFunctor`. So the definition is Mathlib's general singular homology functor evaluated at integer coefficients, giving the degree-n homology of the singular chain complex with ℤ coefficients. On a continuous map it gives the induced homology map, as the `rfl` lemma `integralSingularHomologyFunctor_map` confirms. The universe lift changes nothing mathematically, since `ULift ℤ` is isomorphic to ℤ. Fixing ℤ as the coefficients is what "integral singular homology" means, so this is a specific object, not an overly narrow one.
